stem: A body of mass \(m\) moving along a straight line covers half the distance with a speed of \(2\,\text{m s}^{-1}\). The remaining half of the distance is covered in two equal time intervals with a speed of \(3\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) and \(5\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) respectively. The average speed of the particle for the entire journey is
solution:
Second half: equal TIME intervals at \(3\) and \(5\,\text{m s}^{-1}\), so its average speed is \(\dfrac{3+5}{2} = 4\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
The two halves are equal DISTANCES at \(v_1 = 2\) and \(v_2 = 4\), so the overall average is the harmonic form:
\(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2} = \dfrac{2 \times 2 \times 4}{2+4} = \dfrac{16}{6} = \dfrac{8}{3}\,\text{m s}^{-1}\)
Matches option B.

stem: A motorboat covers a given distance in 6 hours moving downstream on a river. It covers the same distance in 10 hours moving upstream. The time it takes to cover the same distance in still water is
solution:
Let the distance be \(d\), boat speed in still water \(v\), river speed \(u\).
Downstream: \(v + u = \dfrac{d}{6}\). Upstream: \(v - u = \dfrac{d}{10}\).
Adding: \(2v = \dfrac{d}{6} + \dfrac{d}{10} = \dfrac{8d}{30}\), so \(v = \dfrac{2d}{15}\).
Time in still water \(= \dfrac{d}{v} = \dfrac{15}{2} = 7.5\) hours.
Matches option B.

stem: A car moves from \(A\) to \(B\) with a speed of 30 kmph and from \(B\) to \(A\) with a speed of 20 kmph. What is the average speed of the car?
solution:
Equal distances one way and back, so \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}\).
\(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2 \times 30 \times 20}{30+20} = \dfrac{1200}{50} = 24\) kmph
Matches option D.

stem: The velocity - time graph for two bodies \(A\) and \(B\) are shown. Then the acceleration of \(A\) and \(B\) are in the ratio
solution:
Acceleration is the slope of a velocity-time graph, i.e. \(\tan\) of the angle the line makes with the TIME axis.
Line \(A\) makes \(25^\circ\) with the time axis, so \(a_A = \tan 25^\circ\).
The \(40^\circ\) for line \(B\) is marked from the VELOCITY axis, so \(B\) makes \(90^\circ - 40^\circ = 50^\circ\) with the time axis: \(a_B = \tan 50^\circ\).
\(a_A : a_B = \tan 25^\circ : \tan 50^\circ\)
Matches option A.

stem: A body falls freely for 10 s. Its average velocity during this journey (take \(g = 10\,\text{m s}^{-2}\))
solution:
Starting from rest, \(v = gt = 10 \times 10 = 100\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) after 10 s.
Uniform acceleration, so \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{0 + 100}{2} = 50\,\text{m s}^{-1}\)
Matches option C.

stem: A car moving with a velocity of \(20\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) is stopped in a distance of 40 m. If the same car is travelling at double the velocity, the distance travelled by it for same retardation is
solution:
Stopping: \(0 = u^2 - 2as\), so \(s = \dfrac{u^2}{2a}\), i.e. \(s \propto u^2\) at fixed retardation.
Doubling \(u\) multiplies \(s\) by 4: \(s' = 4 \times 40 = 160\,\text{m}\)
Matches option D.

stem: At a metro station, a girl walks up a stationary escalator in 20 s. If she remains stationary on the escalator, then the escalator take her up in 30 s. The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be
solution:
Let the escalator length be \(L\). Her speed \(= \dfrac{L}{20}\), the escalator's speed \(= \dfrac{L}{30}\).
Walking on the moving escalator the speeds add: \(\dfrac{L}{20} + \dfrac{L}{30} = \dfrac{5L}{60} = \dfrac{L}{12}\).
Time \(= 12\,\text{s}\)
Matches option A.

stem: The velocity \((v)\) of a particle starting from rest increases linearly with time \((t)\) as \(v = 4t\), where \(v\) is in \(\text{m s}^{-1}\) and \(t\) is in second. The distance covered by the particle in the first 4 seconds is
solution:
\(v = 4t\) gives a constant acceleration \(a = 4\,\text{m s}^{-2}\), from rest.
\(s = \dfrac{1}{2}at^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4^2 = 32\,\text{m}\)
Matches option B.

stem: Two bodies of masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are dropped from two different heights \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) respectively. The ratio of the times taken by the two masses to touch the ground is (neglect air resistance)
solution:
Free fall from rest: \(h = \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\), so \(t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}\), independent of mass.
\(\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{h_1}{h_2}}\)
Matches option D.

stem: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) with the time axis. The ratio of their velocities is
solution:
Velocity is the slope of a displacement-time graph: \(v = \tan\theta\).
\(v_1 : v_2 = \tan 30^\circ : \tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} : 1 = 1 : \sqrt{3}\)
Matches option D.

stem: A body starts from the rest and acquires a velocity of 10 m/s in 2 s. What is the acceleration of the body and the distance travelled
solution:
\(a = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{10 - 0}{2} = 5\,\text{m/s}^2\)
\(s = \dfrac{1}{2}at^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 2^2 = 10\,\text{m}\)
Matches option A.

stem: An airplane flies 400 m north and 300 m south and flies 1200 m upward, then net displacement is
solution:
North-south: \(400 - 300 = 100\,\text{m}\) north. Vertical: \(1200\,\text{m}\) up. The two are perpendicular.
\(|\vec{s}| = \sqrt{100^2 + 1200^2} = \sqrt{1450000} \approx 1204\,\text{m}\)
The nearest printed value is \(1200\,\text{m}\).
Matches option C.
reviewNote: Exact net displacement is about 1204 m, which is not printed; keyed 1200 m (C) as the nearest value, the standard textbook answer. Owner approved keying C.

stem: A car moving with uniform acceleration covers the distance of 200 m in first 2 seconds and the distance of 220 m in next 4 seconds. The velocity of the car after 7 seconds is
solution:
Use \(s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2\) from the start.
First 2 s: \(200 = 2u + 2a\), so \(u + a = 100\).
First 6 s: \(200 + 220 = 6u + 18a\), so \(u + 3a = 70\).
Subtracting: \(2a = -30\), \(a = -15\,\text{m s}^{-2}\), and \(u = 115\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
\(v = u + at = 115 - 15 \times 7 = 10\,\text{m s}^{-1}\)
Matches option A.

stem: A particle moves along a straight line along the x-axis. Its position \((x)\) versus time \((t)\) graph is shown in the figure [\(x\) in meters and \(t\) in seconds]. Its average speed during this motion is
solution:
Read the graph: \(x = 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 3\,\text{m}\) at \(t = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\,\text{s}\).
Path length: \(0\) to \(2\,\text{s}\) moves \(2\,\text{m}\); \(2\) to \(3\,\text{s}\) at rest; \(3\) to \(4\,\text{s}\) back \(1\,\text{m}\); \(4\) to \(5\,\text{s}\) forward \(1\,\text{m}\).
Total distance \(= 2 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 4\,\text{m}\) in \(5\,\text{s}\).
Average speed \(= \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8\,\text{m s}^{-1}\)
Matches option C.

stem: The velocity of a particle is given by \(v = 2t^2 - 8t + 15\,\text{m s}^{-1}\). Find its instantaneous acceleration at \(t = 5\,\text{s}\).
solution:
\(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = 4t - 8\)
At \(t = 5\,\text{s}\): \(a = 20 - 8 = 12\,\text{m s}^{-2}\)
Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following options is correct for the object having a straight-line motion represented by the following graph?
optA: The object moves with constantly increasing velocity from \(O\) to \(A\) and then it moves with constant velocity.
optB: Velocity of the object increases uniformly.
solution:
The graph plots time on the vertical axis against position \(s\) on the horizontal axis, with time always increasing along the path \(O \to A \to B \to C \to D\).
The path starts at \(O\) (\(s = 0\)) and ends at \(D\), which lies on the time axis, so \(s = 0\) again.
Net displacement is zero, so the average velocity (displacement divided by time) is zero.
Time never runs backwards along the path, so the motion is possible; and the slopes change from segment to segment, so the velocity is neither uniformly increasing nor constant.
Matches option C.

stem: A ball projected up passes the same height \(H\) at 2 s and 10 s. The value of \(H\) is [Use \(g = 9.8\,\text{m/s}^2\)]
solution:
\(H = ut - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\) has roots \(t_1 = 2\) and \(t_2 = 10\), so their product is \(t_1t_2 = \dfrac{2H}{g}\).
\(H = \dfrac{1}{2}g\,t_1t_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times 20 = 98\,\text{m}\)
Matches option C.

stem: A stone falls freely such that the distance covered by it in the last second of its motion is equal to the distance covered by it in the first 5 s. It is in air for ______ s.
solution:
Distance in the \(n\)th second from rest: \(s_n = \dfrac{g}{2}(2n - 1)\).
Distance in the first 5 s: \(\dfrac{1}{2}g \times 5^2 = \dfrac{g}{2} \times 25\).
Equating: \(2n - 1 = 25\), so \(n = 13\,\text{s}\)
Matches option B.

stem: Preeti reached the metro station and found that the escalator was not working. She walked up the stationary escalator in time \(t_1\). On other days, if she remains stationary on the moving escalator, then the escalator takes her up in time \(t_2\). The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be
solution:
Let the escalator length be \(L\). Her speed \(= \dfrac{L}{t_1}\), the escalator's speed \(= \dfrac{L}{t_2}\).
Together: \(v = \dfrac{L}{t_1} + \dfrac{L}{t_2} = \dfrac{L(t_1 + t_2)}{t_1t_2}\).
\(t = \dfrac{L}{v} = \dfrac{t_1t_2}{t_1 + t_2}\)
Matches option B.

stem: A stone falls freely under gravity. It covers distances \(h_1\), \(h_2\) and \(h_3\) in the first 5 seconds, the next 5 seconds and the next 5 seconds respectively. The relation between \(h_1\), \(h_2\) and \(h_3\) is
solution:
Total fallen after 5, 10, 15 s: \(\dfrac{1}{2}g(5)^2\), \(\dfrac{1}{2}g(10)^2\), \(\dfrac{1}{2}g(15)^2\), in the ratio \(1 : 4 : 9\).
So the successive intervals are in the ratio \(h_1 : h_2 : h_3 = 1 : (4 - 1) : (9 - 4) = 1 : 3 : 5\).
Hence \(h_1 = \dfrac{h_2}{3} = \dfrac{h_3}{5}\)
Matches option D.

stem: The motion of a particle along a straight line is described by equation \(x = 8 + 12t - t^3\) where \(x\) is in metre and \(t\) in second. The retardation of the particle when its velocity becomes zero is
solution:
\(v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 12 - 3t^2\), which is zero at \(t = 2\,\text{s}\).
\(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = -6t = -12\,\text{m s}^{-2}\) at \(t = 2\,\text{s}\).
The negative acceleration is a retardation of \(12\,\text{m s}^{-2}\)
Matches option D.

stem: A particle moves in a straight line with a constant acceleration. It changes its velocity from \(10\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) to \(20\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) while passing through a distance 135 m in \(t\) second. The value of \(t\) is
solution:
At constant acceleration, \(s = \dfrac{u + v}{2}\,t\).
\(135 = \dfrac{10 + 20}{2}\,t = 15t\), so \(t = 9\,\text{s}\)
Matches option B.

stem: A car moves from \(X\) to \(Y\) with a uniform speed \(v_u\) and returns to \(X\) with a uniform speed \(v_d\). The average speed for this round trip is
solution:
Let \(XY = d\). Time out \(= \dfrac{d}{v_u}\), time back \(= \dfrac{d}{v_d}\).
\(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{\dfrac{d}{v_u} + \dfrac{d}{v_d}} = \dfrac{2v_dv_u}{v_d + v_u}\)
Matches option D.
reviewNote: Printed stem says 'returns to Y'; corrected to 'returns to X' (obvious typo, owner approved). Semantic duplicate of bank row bcdd695e (half-distance average speed, same option set).

stem: Motion of a particle is given by equation \(s = (3t^3 + 7t^2 + 14t + 8)\,\text{m}\). The value of acceleration of the particle at \(t = 1\,\text{s}\) is
solution:
\(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 9t^2 + 14t + 14\)
\(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = 18t + 14\)
At \(t = 1\,\text{s}\): \(a = 18 + 14 = 32\,\text{m/s}^2\)
Matches option B.

stem: The position \(x\) of a particle varies with time \((t)\) as \(x = at^2 - bt^3\). The acceleration will be zero at time \(t\) is equal to
solution:
\(v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2at - 3bt^2\)
\(\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 2a - 6bt = 0\), so \(t = \dfrac{a}{3b}\)
Matches option A.
